h1: The 7 Best Ink Tank Printers for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ink Tank Printers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best ink tank printers for home offices, from budget EcoTank models to ADF and Ethernet picks.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-4850 is the most complete office machine here, with scanner, copier, fax, ADF and Ethernet. The ET-4950 suits steady printers who want a long stretch between refills, and the ET-2800 is the cheapest sensible way into ink tank printing. HP's Smart Tank 5101 is the one alternative to the Epson line.
intro: The biggest mistake home office buyers make with ink tank printers is paying for features they never touch. A fax port and a document feeder sound useful until you realize you scan one page a week, and the cheaper model would have done the same job.

We ranked seven ink tank printers on the spec sheets and listing details: how much office hardware each includes, how it connects, and how much ink you start with. We left out the white ET-2800 because it is the same printer as the black one in a different finish.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4850 Supertank with Scanner, Copier, Fax, ADF, and Ethernet
products.verdict: Every office feature a home worker could want, without a cartridge in sight.
products.description:
The ET-4850 is a cartridge-free ink tank printer that bundles a scanner, copier, fax, automatic document feeder and Ethernet port. It sits in the $200-500 bracket and is clearly built with an office desk in mind rather than a family living room.

It ranks first because it is the only pick here that lists all of those office tools together. The ET-3850 above it in price tier drops fax, and the ET-4800 keeps fax but sits in a cheaper bracket. You pay more than for the ET-2800, and what you buy is paperwork handling.

Choose it if you scan multi-page contracts, send the occasional fax, or want a wired network connection. Skip it if you only print a few pages a week, because the extra hardware is wasted on you.
products.idealFor: A home office that scans, copies and occasionally faxes multi-page documents.
products.skipIf: You print a handful of pages a week and never scan.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4950 Supertank Printer, Up to 3 Years of Ink
products.verdict: The longest stretch between refills of anything in this ranking.
products.description:
The ET-4950 ships with up to three years of ink, a 2.4-inch color touchscreen, an automatic document feeder and an 18 PPM print speed. It lives in the $200-500 bracket alongside the other premium EcoTank models.

It lands just below the ET-4850 because it lists no fax or Ethernet, while the ET-4850 does. In return you get the touchscreen and the most generous starting ink supply, which matters more if you print every day.

Best for steady printers who hate buying ink bottles. The caveat is that the ink advantage only pays off if your volume is high enough to use it.
products.idealFor: Daily printers who want to go years without buying ink.
products.skipIf: You need fax or a wired network connection.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-3850 Supertank Printer with Ethernet and ADF
products.verdict: Ethernet and a document feeder without paying for fax or a touchscreen.
products.description:
The ET-3850 pairs a cartridge-free tank system with Ethernet, an automatic document feeder, mobile printing support and a built-in scanner and copier. A bonus black ink bottle and a USB cable come in the box.

It ranks under the ET-4850 because it lacks fax, and under the ET-4950 because it lists no extended ink supply. It beats the ET-4800 below for higher-volume offices since it sits in the premium bracket and is aimed at heavier use.

Pick it if you want a wired connection and a feeder and have no need for fax. The caveat is that it costs more than entry models that do the same everyday printing.
products.idealFor: Higher-volume offices that want a wired, shared printer.
products.skipIf: You only connect over Wi-Fi and rarely scan.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer with Fax and Ethernet
products.verdict: Fax, feeder and Ethernet in a cheaper bracket than the premium models.
products.description:
The ET-4800 offers a cartridge-free tank system, automatic document feeder, fax and Ethernet, with wireless connectivity too. It sits in the $100-200 bracket, which is unusual for a machine with this many office tools.

It ranks below the ET-3850 and ET-4950 because they sit in a heavier-duty tier, but it is the better value of the group if you need fax. Compared with the ET-2800 below, you gain the feeder and a wired connection.

Good for a small office that wants real paperwork tools on a tighter budget. The caveat is that the listing gives no extended ink supply, so expect to buy refills sooner than with the ET-4950.
products.idealFor: Small offices that want fax and a feeder on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want the largest starting ink supply.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer, Black
products.verdict: The cheapest sensible entry into cartridge-free printing for a home office.
products.description:
The ET-2800 is a wireless color all-in-one with scan and copy, a cartridge-free tank system and visible ink levels on the front panel. It is compact and sits in the $100-200 bracket.

It ranks below the ET-4800 because it has no document feeder, Ethernet or fax. It ranks above the ET-2400 because it is the better-documented model for office duty, with ink levels you can read at a glance.

Best for moderate monthly volume where scanning means one page at a time. The caveat is that you scan and copy by hand, sheet by sheet.
products.idealFor: Moderate printers who want low running costs on a budget.
products.skipIf: You scan stacks of pages or need Ethernet.

products.name: HP Smart Tank 5101 Wireless Refillable All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: The HP answer to the ET-2800, with two years of ink in the box.
products.description:
The Smart Tank 5101 is a refillable ink tank all-in-one with a scanner and copier, wireless connectivity on 2.4GHz only, and two years of ink included. It sits in the $100-200 bracket.

It ranks below the ET-2800 because that Epson lists clearer office-friendly details such as front-panel ink levels. Its two-year ink supply is its strongest argument against the ET-2400 below.

Choose it if you already use the HP ecosystem. The caveat is the 2.4GHz-only Wi-Fi, which can matter on modern 5GHz-only networks.
products.idealFor: Light-to-moderate printers who prefer HP software.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2400 Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A bare-bones ink tank printer for very light offices.
products.description:
The ET-2400 is a compact, wireless, cartridge-free all-in-one with scan and copy, positioned for everyday home printing. Its price falls between $100 and $200.

It closes the list because its listing details are thinner than the ET-2800's, with no mention of front-panel ink levels. Otherwise the two offer a similar core feature set.

Best for very light home offices. The caveat is that the spec sheet is sparse, so confirm connectivity details before buying.
products.idealFor: Very light users wanting cheap ink tank printing.
products.skipIf: You need office extras like a feeder.

methodology.title: Office hardware
methodology.description: We checked which models list a document feeder, fax and Ethernet, since these separate office printers from family ones.

methodology.title: Ink supply
methodology.description: We compared what ink comes with the printer, from standard bottles to up to three years.

methodology.title: Connectivity
methodology.description: We weighed wired Ethernet and Wi-Fi band support, which decide how easily the printer joins a home network.

methodology.title: Convenience features
methodology.description: Touchscreens, front-panel ink levels and print speed counted toward daily usability.

methodology.title: Price bracket
methodology.description: Each model was judged against the bracket it sits in, so a cheaper pick is not punished for lacking premium extras.

whatMatters.detail: An ADF pulls multi-page documents through the scanner without you lifting the lid for each sheet. It matters because scanning a ten-page contract by hand is slow. Check the listing for 'ADF' or 'automatic document feeder' in the spec bullets, since entry models usually omit it.

Ethernet gives a stable wired link that does not drop when the router is busy. It matters if the printer sits far from the router or is shared between machines. Look for an Ethernet port in the specs rather than assuming a premium model has one.

Some printers include enough ink for up to three years of typical use. That reduces early refills, which is the whole appeal of an ink tank. Read the box contents on the listing to see how many bottles come included.
A printer limited to 2.4GHz cannot join a router set to 5GHz only. It matters because many modern routers separate bands. Check the listing for the supported Wi-Fi band before you buy.
Tanks with a visible level window let you refill before running dry. This prevents mid-job failures. Look for 'front panel tank levels' in the specs.

howToChoose.intro: Match the printer to what you actually do at your desk.

cards.label: Wired Ethernet
cards.text: A cable link is steadier for a shared office printer. The ET-4850, ET-3850 and ET-4800 include Ethernet.

cards.label: Wireless only
cards.text: Simpler to place anywhere in the room. The ET-2800, ET-2400 and HP Smart Tank 5101 are Wi-Fi only.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to wireless unless the printer sits far from the router or serves several computers.

rows: Two years of ink in the box

cards.text: A compact body and a front-panel layout that does not need rear access.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 and ET-2400 are the compact designs listed, so they suit tight desks best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You scan stacks of paper or print every day. The ET-4850 and ET-4950 add the feeder and ink supply that justify the premium.

cards.text: You print a few pages a week. The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 covers the basics for much less.

faq.q: Do ink tank printers use cartridges?
faq.a: No. Ink tank printers such as the EcoTank line are refilled from bottles into built-in tanks. That is why they are called cartridge-free.

faq.q: Is the white ET-2800 different from the black one?
faq.a: The listing shows the same features in a white finish. We included only the black model to avoid a duplicate entry.

faq.q: Is an ink tank printer worth it over a cartridge printer?
faq.a: If you print regularly, ink tanks are designed to lower running costs through refill bottles. If you print rarely, the savings matter less.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Fill each tank from its matching bottle, then connect over Wi-Fi or Ethernet using the manufacturer's app. Models with a USB cable in the box can also connect directly.

faq.q: How do I keep the ink flowing?
faq.a: Print something occasionally, and check the tank levels on the front panel where the model has them. Refill before a tank runs low.

faq.q: Can the HP Smart Tank 5101 join my 5GHz network?
faq.a: Its listing says 2.4GHz only, so it will not connect to a router that only broadcasts 5GHz. Check your router settings first.

finalTake: For a full-service home office, the Epson EcoTank ET-4850 is the safest buy. If your volume is high and you hate refills, the ET-4950 earns its place. Most light users will be happy with the ET-2800, and the savings over the premium models are real.
